hook: Thomas Cover was born in San Bernardino, California, in 1938. He earned a BS in physics from MIT in 1960 and then moved to Stanford, completing an MS in 1961 and a PhD in electrical engineering in 1964. He joined the Stanford faculty the same year and remained there for the rest of his career, holding a joint appointment in electrical engineering and statistics. In 1967 he and Peter Hart published Nearest Neighbor Pattern Classification, proving that a simple rule of comparing a new example to its closest labeled neighbors could not do much worse than the best possible classifier, a result that became a founding theorem of pattern recognition. He went on to make major contributions to broadcast channel coding and portfolio theory, and in 1991 he and Joy Thomas published Elements of Information Theory, which became the standard graduate textbook in the field. He died at Stanford Hospital on March 26, 2012, at age 73.

achievements.title: Nearest Neighbor Pattern Classification (1967)
achievements.impact: Proved fundamental bounds on the error rate of the nearest neighbor rule with Peter Hart, giving pattern recognition one of its first rigorous theoretical foundations and a widely used algorithm.

achievements.title: Elements of Information Theory (1991)
achievements.impact: Co-written with Joy Thomas, it became the standard graduate textbook in information theory and introduced generations of students and researchers to the field.

achievements.title: Broadcast channel superposition coding (1973)
achievements.impact: Introduced a coding approach that let a single transmitter send information to multiple receivers simultaneously, a foundational idea in network information theory.

achievements.title: IEEE Claude E. Shannon Award (1990) and Richard W. Hamming Medal (1997)
achievements.impact: Recognized him as one of the leading information theorists of his generation.
